[1/4] Plan boarding and prize capture: a marine-gated combat action that turns a crippled hostile into a fleet prize, with CLI/cockpit parity, browser review and codex progression.

impact_assessment.why: Combat offers only destruction; the marine crew role has no active use, and the fleet manager has no combat-driven growth path.
impact_assessment.benefits: Crippled enemies become a tactical choice: finish them for bounty or board for a lasting escort. Marines gain an active role, and fleet composition can grow from play.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new combat action must stay discoverable through CLI, REST, click map and AI catalog; dependency: no new libraries; concurrency: capture mutates crew injury, morale, fleet ships, stats and active combat in one state clone; state: prize ships must round-trip through saves and a failed boarding must not end combat.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add engine, CLI, layout and browser-scenario tests first; gate boarding on shields, hull and marine; include prize defaults in FleetShip; verify save round-trip and a live Edge click; then run the full suite and gates.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Boarding/prize engine action, marine injury failure path, save round-trip and Privateer codex metric implemented with combat regressions.
[3/4] CLI combat board aliases, gated cockpit button and boarding browser scenario added; live Edge click captured a 20-hull prize and click map shows 136 controls with no gaps.
[4/4] README, COCKPIT guide and ADR-089 recorded; 798 tests pass. checklists: passed
Task 'boarding-prizes' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan prize liquidation: value captured escorts, sell them at a drydock through CLI/REST/cockpit, track Shipbreaker progression, and restore the escort ledger layout.

impact_assessment.why: Boarding creates prizes, but the fleet manager only repairs or dismisses them; captured value cannot be converted to credits, and the third action broke the escort row layout.
impact_assessment.benefits: Prizes become a keep-or-sell decision, the fleet manager gains an economy loop, and the row stays readable at desktop and short widths.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new endpoint must be discoverable and AI-documented; dependency: none; concurrency: sale mutates credits, fleet ships, stats and log in one clone; state: sale must refuse outside a dock and preserve old saves without sale_value.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add engine/API/CLI/layout tests first, centralize the value formula in fleet.py, expose sale_value in both fleet reports, use explicit grid placement for the three actions, and verify a live Edge sale.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Escort sale value, drydock sale, /api/fleet/escort/sell, CLI/REPL parity, Shipbreaker codex and fleet report sale_value implemented with regressions.
[3/3] SELL control and explicit escort-row grid placement fixed; README, COCKPIT guide and ADR-090 recorded. Live Edge sale moved 1000 to 1680 cr; 805 tests and 5/5 gates pass. checklists: passed
Task 'prize-sales' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan local fleet deployment: only stationed escorts fight, remote patrols survive and cut piracy, and fleet reports distinguish local from total strength.

impact_assessment.why: Escort assignment is cosmetic: every ship joins every battle and can die in a system where it is not stationed, while remote patrols provide no benefit.
impact_assessment.benefits: Assignment becomes a real defensive choice, remote ships survive local fights, patrols reduce piracy, and fleet strength readouts tell the truth.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: fleet reports gain fields and UI labels; dependency: none; concurrency: local battle updates must merge into the full roster without dropping remote ships or prizes; state: old saves keep assigned_system_id defaults and zero patrols.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add helper and combat regressions first, pin remote survival and local damage, merge by id with extra prizes retained, expose local totals in both reports, and verify the fleet card labels in real Edge.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Local-only combat selection, remote-safe merge, local/total fleet reporting and patrol piracy reduction implemented with five fleet regressions.
[3/3] Fleet cards show SYS and LOCAL/PATROL, README/COCKPIT and ADR-091 are recorded, 810 tests and 5/5 gates pass. checklists: passed
Task 'fleet-patrol' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan outpost production modules: install up to three stacks, scale cost by stack, expose the catalog, and wire engine/API/CLI/cockpit with regressions.

impact_assessment.why: The outpost module catalog and production multiplier exist, but no action or control can install a module; outposts only level up.
impact_assessment.benefits: Outposts gain horizontal growth, module content becomes reachable, and the Empire tab gets a working credit-to-production loop.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new endpoint must be AI-documented and click-map safe; dependency: none; concurrency: module install mutates outposts and credits in one clone; state: stack counts and catalog must survive saves and old outposts without modules.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add engine, API, CLI and layout tests first; cap stacks at three; expose the catalog in static snapshots; verify a live Edge module install and refresh the knowledge base.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Outpost module installation, three-stack cap, escalating cost, API/CLI parity, static module catalog and regressions implemented.
